title: Connection-pool multiplication
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Multiply per-instance pools during scaling; detect aggregate database-connection exhaustion.
sourceBehavior: Keep aggregate database connections within limits as frontend/API instance counts increase.
sourceAcceptance: Total connections stay within the approved data-tier limit; connection exhaustion and journey latency are detected.
preconditions: Open local HTML in a JavaScript-enabled browser; no server, account, authentication or installation.
Baseline is one frontend and one API instance; at least one tier must scale out.
Every modeled pool is simultaneously saturated to its configured maximum.
The declared connection limit and journey budget are synthetic inputs, not real approval or a platform quota.
Two required checkpoint observations form the fixed denominator.
actions: Choose target tier counts, per-instance pools, synthetic connection limit, journey budget and observation preset.
Observe the baseline, then scale and observe aggregate connections and synthetic journey latency.
Compare a 140-request exhaustion case with a 70-request tuned-pool recovery.
Check a prediction separately from measured success, failure or unknown.
Retain up to six attempts without pruning, or explicitly reset all defaults and history.
syntheticInput: learning/S062/model.js: bounded pure deterministic saturation and latency rules
assertions: Demand equals frontend instances times frontend pool plus API instances times API pool.
Only observed connections and latency can establish a successful checkpoint.
Refused connections or journey latency over budget visibly fail; equality at both budgets passes.
A withheld scaled sample remains unknown, even with a known over-limit configured forecast.
Known failure dominates missing or pending evidence and never disappears from retained history.
Strict input, exact journal shape, phase, payload and retention guards reject without state mutation.
Keyboard controls, explicit reset, handled errors and restrictive CSP work in the actual browser.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine callable-stub assertion RED and before implementation.
iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson; no infrastructure, cloud or deployment authorized.

limits: No actual database connection, pool saturation, instance scaling or connection-exhaustion proof.
Configured maxima become demand only under this explicit synthetic saturation assumption.
Invented latency rules do not predict real journey latency or native database behavior.
Other clients, minimum/idle pools, pool wait queues, traffic skew, retries and dynamic admission are not modeled.
No real authentication, credentials, identity registration, cloud, infrastructure, deployment or spending.
No native, production Node.js 24, source-parent or five-nines certification.
History lasts until reset or reload and is never silently pruned.
B-S062 and D-S062 remain incomplete; parent alone may Accept A-S062.
Published browser helper only; known unattended lifecycle limitation remains and finally close is awaited.
